title: Which page of one large dump holds the most code blocks?
question: DeepWiki returns the documentation of modelcontextprotocol/servers as one markdown dump. The dump is a series of pages. Every page starts with a line of the form '# Page: <title>'. Count only fenced blocks that hold code, so skip every fenced block opened with three backticks and the word mermaid. Find the page that holds the most code blocks. Give its exact title, and copy the first line of that page that starts with two hash marks and a space.
why: ONE call, 392,601 bytes (383.4 KiB). No fan-out, nothing to run in parallel, nothing to loop over. This task exists to isolate the payload term from the fan-out term, which every other task in the set confounds. If code mode wins here, it wins on payload size alone.
extraArmsWhy: The payload is over Claude Code's MCP output limit, so the direct arms that every sweep runs never see it. A-files is the direct arm a real session is: it can open the file. A-raw raises the limit, so the payload enters the window and its cost is counted. Without these two, a code mode win here only says that code mode reached the data. Added 2026-09-22.

predictions.recorded: 2026-09-22, before the first run of A-files and A-raw
predictions.B-uncached vs A-raw: code mode reads at least ten times fewer input tokens. Whether A-raw answers correctly is uncertain.
predictions.B-uncached vs A-files: code mode is cheaper at list price. Whether A-files answers correctly is uncertain.

mayNotCompleteWhy: 392,601 bytes of text is about 103,000 to 119,000 estimated tokens. That is over Claude Code's 25,000 token MCP output limit, so A-uncached and A-cached get a file path instead of the text, and they have no tool to open a file. A-files can open it, and may run out of turns paging through it. A-raw puts the whole payload in the window and resends it every turn, and may run out of budget. Each outcome is a measurement. Rewritten 2026-09-22: the first version said the payload might not fit a 200K window, but the run showed the output limit stops it first.

expect.note: Both strings are DeepWiki's own page and heading names, not repository text. GitHub code search returns zero hits for them inside modelcontextprotocol/servers, so a model cannot produce them from memory. Neither appears in the question: it says 'two hash marks and a space' rather than printing the marker. Margin: 18 code blocks against 15, then a cliff to 5.
